messages:
Sasha: Heads up — seeing DNS timeouts from GPU pods during large-batch jobs in us-west-2. P95 resolve for internal service names jumped from 10ms -> 800ms and a few failed requests.
Miguel: can you paste a sample pod log? which service?
Sasha: grpc calls to model-router.svc.cluster.local failing with: 
```
E0421 10:12:34.123 rpc_client.cc:221] resolve failed: DNS timeout after 5s
E0421 10:12:34.124 batching.cc:88] request aborted due to name resolution error
```
Priya: Any network-wide events? RDMA flaps or recent ToR firmware changes?
Sasha: No RDMA alerts. Noticed increased UDP fragments on the node where the pods ran. tcpdump showed a lot of 'IP fragment' entries and ICMP frag-needed from 10.0.1.1 (tor)
Ben: That smells like MTU mismatch between node NIC and leaf switch. We pushed flow offload kernel tweak last week — could be related.
Leo: I ran a quick dig from a problematic node: 
```
$ dig +short @10.0.0.10 model-router.svc.cluster.local
; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
Sasha: node-local-dns is configured but falling back to CoreDNS after repeated UDP failures, which adds ~1s per lookup when it switches to TCP.
Miguel: Do we have counts for truncated responses (TC bit) from CoreDNS?
Sasha: From a packet capture: many UDP DNS responses > 1200 bytes getting fragmented. Example: DNS UDP length 1850, frag offsets non-zero. Reassembly fails intermittently.
Priya: On RDMA paths, some switches drop fragmented UDP for performance. If the response crosses an RDMA-enabled link with smaller effective MTU we hit this.
Ben: Workaround options: 1) force DNS over TCP in node-local (worse perf), 2) reduce EDNS buffer size to avoid >1200, 3) fix MTU mismatch ASAP.
Leo: EDNS resize is low-risk and quick to test. We can add `edns-udp-size 512` to CoreDNS upstream stub? (or client side via nodelocal config).
Sasha: Trying edns tweak on a single kube node now. Patch applied to nodelocal-configmap: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  stubDomains: |
    {"cluster.local": ["10.0.0.10"]}
  upstreamResolvers: "10.0.0.10"
  edns_udp_size: "512"
```
infra-oncall: Patch queued on one node (gpu-pool-12). Rolling to two more for canary. :white_check_mark:
monitor-bot: cpu/gpu-job-failures spike metric: +14% since 10:00 UTC (correlates).
Miguel: If canary looks good, we should coordinate a ToR/firmware rollback with network team. Also open a ticket for NIC offload rollback (flowtable) on that kernel patch.
Priya: Also add a short-term ipfrag logging tweak so we can see reassembly timeouts: 
```
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ipfrag_high_thresh
# (collect logs for 1 hour)
```
Ben: Note: changing ipfrag thresholds can increase memory usage. keep it short.
Sasha: Canary results: after edns_udp_size 512, resolve p95 back to ~12ms on gpu-pool-12 and no more gRPC DNS failures in last 30m.
Leo: Great. Let's keep EDNS change cluster-wide and schedule infra change window to fix MTU with network.
Miguel: I'll file the network rollback ticket and a postmortem template. Assigning to @neteng.
Sasha: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: add a check in GPU node bootstrap to verify MTU path to ToR and fail early.
Ben: +1. Will write kube-probe script and include in next node image build.
infra-oncall: Marked incident as mitigated, monitoring for 2h. :eyes:
Sasha: closing out here unless anyone sees new failures.
